caveats: This is a structured case study, not a statistically validated causal finding. One company over one date range yields too few distinct incidents for the sentiment/abnormal-return relationship to carry statistical significance; a proper event study spans dozens of companies and events.
Flagged days are days on which unusual coverage COINCIDED WITH an unusual benchmark-adjusted return. Coincidence in time is not evidence that an article caused a price move.

4 flagged day(s) show a price move in the opposite direction to the coverage's tone. That is not necessarily an error: news can be already priced in, or the day's move driven by something the coverage did not capture.

sentiment_return_correlation.note: Pearson r over 64 news-carrying day(s) in this run; descriptive only, not a significance test, and not comparable across runs with different day counts.

sentiment_extremity_volume_correlation.note: Pearson r over 64 news-carrying day(s) between |sentiment| and volume's own z-score; descriptive only, not a significance test.

1.note: Pearson r over 64 pair(s) of (day t sentiment, day t+1 abnormal return); descriptive only, not a significance test.

5.note: Pearson r over 64 pair(s) of (day t sentiment, day t+5 abnormal return); descriptive only, not a significance test.

emotion_return_summary.note: 12 day(s) had a confident dominant emotion (GoEmotions, headline-only, secondary to FinBERT); grouped by the paper's own positive/negative/ambiguous clustering. Descriptive only — small day counts per group, and this never affects incident flagging or ranking.

threshold_robustness.note: each candidate day's flagging test re-run across 9 combinations of coverage/return z-thresholds (0.7x/1x/1.3x of the 1/1.5 configured values). A day flagged in all combinations is robust to the exact threshold chosen; one flagged in only the loosest combination is threshold-sensitive - treat it with more caution.

headlines.summary: Zydus Lifesciences will roll out generic semaglutide injections in India post-patent expiry, using a reusable single-pen device to improve affordability and patient adherence.

headlines.headline: Zydus plans launch of semaglutide generic in reusable pen form
headlines.summary: Zydus Lifesciences is set to launch a generic version of the weight-loss injection semaglutide next month. The drug will be available under brand names Semaglyn, Mashema, and Altreme. Zydus will offer a unique reusable pen for easier dosage adjustment. This move aims to simplify treatment for patients managing Type 2 diabetes and obesity.

headlines.headline: Zydus Lifesciences shares fall 2% as firm acquires US-based Assertio Holdings for $166 million

This strategic move aims to enhance the company's innovative drug offerings.
